value: STANDESAMT BERLIN-WEDDING, STERBEREGISTER 1943, NR. 1291. Landesarchiv Berlin, P Rep. 830 Nr. 114. Scanned and sent by Arabella Oberle, Landesarchiv Berlin, 29 September 2026, in answer to this archive's enquiry. THE OFFICE IS THE ARCHIVIST'S, NOT AN INFERENCE OF MINE — I had worked it out from the hospital's street and was about to publish it as a deduction when the covering letter stated it outright with the shelfmark.
Die Arbeiterin GERTRUD SARA LEIBHOLZ, mosaisch, wohnhaft in Berlin-Charlottenburg, Marburger Straße 13.
27 FEBRUARY 1943, at 08:45, "in Berlin, Iranische Straße 2, im Judenkrankenhause" — the Jewish Hospital in Wedding.
13 July 1894 in Berlin. The registry office of her birth is entered as "Berlin ?" and the number left blank.

field: cause of death, in the registrar's own words
value: *** "SELBSTMORD DURCH ZYANKALIVERGIFTUNG" — SUICIDE BY CYANIDE POISONING. ***

Eingetragen auf [mündliche — struck out] SCHRIFTLICHE Anzeige DES POLIZEIPRÄSIDENTEN IN BERLIN. Not a relative. The archivist notes in her covering letter that police involvement is unremarkable for an unnatural death, and that is right — but the consequence stands: every line about her family is blank.

field: *** AND THE BLANKS ARE THE DOCUMENT ***
value: Vater: "Namen nicht bekannt." Mutter: "Namen nicht bekannt." The words "nicht verheiratet" are STRUCK OUT and replaced by "Familienstand nicht bekannt". The marriage line at the foot has a question mark in every field — date, place, office, number. THE STATE THAT HAD REGISTERED HER AS A JEW, RENAMED HER AND PUT HER TO LABOUR RECORDED THAT IT DID NOT KNOW WHETHER SHE WAS MARRIED.

GERTRUD née LEIBKE, wife of OSKAR LEIBHOLZ, who was Jacob's brother. This archive already held the proof from the other end: the AJDC card for Oskar, DocID 11243228, gives his last address as "BERLIN W 50, MARBURGERSTR. 13" and names "Ehefrau: (Sa) GERTRUD geb. LEIBKE 13.7.94 Berlin". ADDRESS AND DATE OF BIRTH MATCH THE REGISTER EXACTLY. Two documents made by different authorities for different purposes, agreeing to the house number and the day.

field: SARA IS NOT A NAME SHE WAS GIVEN
value: it is the compulsory forename imposed on Jewish women by the Second Decree of 17 August 1938. The same law put "Israel" in the margin of her brother-in-law's marriage entry, scanned in the same email. It is on her death record because it was on her papers.

field: ARBEITERIN IS NOT A TRADE SHE CHOSE
value: a Jewish woman of 48 described as a labourer in Berlin in February 1943 was in Zwangsarbeit — forced labour. The word is the state's.

field: *** THE DATE, AND THIS ARCHIVE IS STATING IT AS CONTEXT AND NOT AS CAUSE ***
value: 27 FEBRUARY 1943 IS THE FABRIKAKTION — the day the Gestapo seized Jewish forced labourers from their workplaces across Berlin. She was a labourer and she died at a quarter to nine that morning. THE REGISTER SAYS WHAT SHE DID AND DOES NOT SAY WHY, AND NOR WILL THIS ARCHIVE. The coincidence of day is recorded because it is a fact about the date and because leaving it out would be its own kind of claim.

26 FEBRUARY 1943 — JACOB LEIBHOLZ, her brother-in-law, deported from Berlin. 27 FEBRUARY 1943, 08:45 — GERTRUD dies. 8 MARCH 1943 — the death registered on the police president's written notice. 17 MARCH 1943 — OSKAR, her husband, deported on the 4. großer Alterstransport to Theresienstadt, EIGHTEEN DAYS AFTER SHE DIED. 1944 — Oskar dies there.

field: AND IT CORRECTS THE GEDENKBUCH'S BOROUGH, MILDLY
value: the Gedenkbuch gives her residence as Berlin (WILMERSDORF) and the register says CHARLOTTENBURG, Marburger Straße 13. Both are right about different years: the census of 17 May 1939 has Oskar and Gertrud at Waghäuseler Straße 9/10, which IS Wilmersdorf. The Gedenkbuch is using the 1939 address and the register the 1943 one. A MOVE, NOT A CONTRADICTION.

her parents, who are not named on any document this archive holds; whether Marburger Straße 13 was a Judenhaus — Oskar's card gives the same address and that is suggestive and is not evidence; and anything whatever about her reasons.
